0.title: The API
0.content: spezado serve offers an open HTTP API under /api/v1 – the same one the web app uses: over HTTP on the device itself, over TLS to other devices (serve --listen). Over TLS the certificate is the workspace’s own; a client checks its fingerprint, which the pairing link carries (#pair=…&fingerprint=sha256:…), instead of a certificate authority. It is described in OpenAPI 3.1: openapi.json, also written by spezado openapi.

1.title: Pairing and tokens
1.content: Every client pairs once with the code serve shows and then sends its token with every request: . curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8048/api/v1/pair \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"code": "6958d36774", "name": "script"}' # {"token": "…", "device": "…"} – the token is shown once curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8048/api/v1/books -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" . GET /api/v1/devices lists the devices paired, DELETE /api/v1/devices/{device} revokes one.

2.title: What it offers
2.content: | Area | Endpoints | . | Books | GET POST /books – list, set up; GET /books/{books}/overview, /journal, /accounts, /balances, /tax-codes | . | Booking | POST /books/{books}/bookings/simple, /bookings/lines, /reversals; GET POST /opening | . | Bank | POST /books/{books}/bank/statements; GET /bank/entries; POST /bank/entries/book, /bank/entries/accept, /bank/accept-all | . | Documents | GET POST /books/{books}/documents; GET /documents/{document}/original | . | Invoices | GET PUT /books/{books}/invoicing/profile; GET POST /customers; POST /invoices; GET /invoices/next-number | . | Reports | GET /books/{books}/reports, /reports/{report}; GET PUT /deadlines; GET /review | . | Closing | POST /books/{books}/closings; GET /gobd | . | Synchronisation | GET POST /books/{books}/sync – status, synchronise now; POST /sync/start, /sync/invitations (with rights); GET /sync/devices, DELETE /sync/devices/{member}; POST /sync/join, /sync/recover | . | Changes | GET /events – Server-Sent Events: changed with the books whenever something was written | . Amounts are written with their currency, the value as a decimal string with a point – {"value": "-12.40", "currency": "EUR"}; amounts sent are decimal strings ("1234.50"), dates YYYY-MM-DD. Errors come as {"error": "…"}, in English, with a status of 400 (a request that cannot be read), 401 (no valid token), 404 or 422 (refused, e.g. a booking that does not balance). A browser, which cannot set headers for an event stream, passes its token as the query token.

8.title: The command line
8.content: Everything the terminal does with books is open to scripts as well. Every command takes --dir (the workspace) and, where the workspace holds several sets of books, --books; spezado help <command> shows its options. | Command |   | . | init | creates a workspace for this device | . | books | lists the books of the workspace | . | set-up | sets up books for a person or an organisation | . | book | records a booking from lines | . | reverse | reverses a booking by the event that recorded it | . | journal, balance | the journal, the balance of every account | . | report | a report for a period, or – without one – the reports that apply | . | check | what needs review | . | close | closes an owner’s books up to a date | . | filing | lists the filings; prepare, submit [--test], refresh (Filings) | . | adapter | shows or sets the adapter that submits filings in a country, the token from SPEZADO_ADAPTER_TOKEN | . | export, import | the events of the books as JSON Lines, out and in | . | sync | synchronises books with other devices and people: start, invite --rights, join, recover, devices, remove (Synchronisation) | . | relay | runs a relay | . | tui, serve | the terminal; the web app and API – serve --listen 0.0.0.0:8443 for other devices, over TLS (The web app) | . | openapi | the description of the API | .

9.title: A freelancer’s quarter
9.content: spezado init spezado set-up --name "Ada" --from 2026-01-01 --accounting de-cash-basis \ --vat de-regular --vat-basis cash --vat-period quarter --chart de-skr03 --region DE-BE spezado book --date 2026-02-10 --text "Invoice 1" 1200=1190 8400=-1000@de-out-19 1776=-190@de-out-19 spezado book --date 2026-02-12 --text "Paper" 4930=10@de-in-19 1576=1.90@de-in-19 1200=-11.90 spezado journal spezado report de-ustva --from 2026-01-01 --to 2026-03-31 spezado check . A line of book is an account – its number in the books’ chart, or its UUID –, =, the amount with a decimal point, positive for debit and negative for credit, and optionally @ and a tax code; the lines must balance. set-up without --legal-form sets up a person’s books; with one (de-gmbh, de-ev, …) an organisation’s. --accounting is de-cash-basis or de-double-entry, --vat de-regular or de-small-business, --chart de-skr03 or de-skr04; --vat-extended and --region (DE-BY, DE-NW, …) move the deadlines. The reports for German books are de-ustva (advance VAT return) and de-euer (Anlage EÜR) on a cash basis, and the balance sheet and profit and loss account after the HGB with double entry.

10.title: Filings
10.content: A filing is what goes to an authority: in Germany the advance VAT return (de-ustva) and the Anlage EÜR (de-euer). spezado derives it from the books, records it, and submits it through an adapter – a service of its own per country that talks to the authority, after librotenado 0007. spezado itself never talks to ELSTER. OPEN: there is no adapter for ELSTER yet. It needs ERiC, the library of the German tax administration, which is handed out to registered developers only; falkOSS registers once it is founded. Until then filings are prepared and recorded, and can be tried with any adapter that follows librotenado 0007.

11.title: Preparing
11.content: A filing is prepared from a report and its period: its fields as the books give them now, and the state of the books they were derived from. It is never changed afterwards. | Asked again while nothing changed, spezado returns the same filing. | When the books change so that the fields would differ – a booking in the period, a reversal –, the filing is outdated: it is not submitted; prepare it again. | A filing prepared after one was submitted or accepted is a correction of it (in German a berichtigte Voranmeldung). | A VAT return with nothing to report is a filing too. | .

12.title: Submitting
12.content: The adapter is set per country: its address – https://…, or http://127.0.0.1:… on this device – and the token spezado authenticates itself with. The token goes into the key store of the system where there is one. A test submission goes to the adapter marked as a test, which the authority does not process; nothing is recorded in the books. A real one moves the filing on: submitted, then accepted or rejected as the authority answers. What it returns – a protocol of the transfer, a notice – becomes a document of the books, with its original. A rejected filing is submitted again, or corrected. |   | Terminal | Web app | Command line | . | prepare | p on a report’s figures | Prepare as a filing on a report | spezado filing prepare de-ustva --from … --to … | . | list | the filings after the reports | Filings under the reports | spezado filing | . | submit | ↵ on a filing: a test or for real | Submit as a test, Submit | spezado filing submit <id> [--test] | . | ask where it stands | ↵ on a submitted filing | Ask where it stands | spezado filing refresh <id> | . | set the adapter | – | Filings, change | SPEZADO_ADAPTER_TOKEN=… spezado adapter DE <url> | .

14.title: Download
14.content: Every release has an archive per platform – Linux (x86_64, arm64), macOS (arm64) and Windows (x86_64) – with a SHA-256 checksum: releases. Unpack it; the archive holds the program spezado (spezado.exe), the licences and the changelog. The web app is built into the program. shasum -a 256 -c spezado-0.3.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz.sha256 tar -xzf spezado-0.3.0-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz ./spezado-0.3.0-aarch64-apple-darwin/spezado tui . The binaries are not signed: macOS and Windows may ask before the first start.

15.title: Build it yourself
15.content: spezado is written in Rust; the toolchain is picked up from rust-toolchain.toml by rustup. The web app needs Node.js and pnpm to be built – without it, serve offers the API alone. git clone https://github.com/spezado/spezado cd spezado (cd web && pnpm install && pnpm build) # the web app, embedded into the binary cargo run --release -- tui # the terminal cargo run --release -- serve # or the web app: open the address it shows .

16.title: The workspace
16.content: A workspace is where this device keeps its books: a SQLite database and the originals of your documents. It lives in spezado’s folder in your data directory, or wherever --dir or the environment variable SPEZADO_DIR say. One workspace holds as many sets of books as you like; --books picks one where there are several.

17.title: The first books
17.content: Start the terminal (spezado tui): without books it asks for them – name, first day, how profit is determined (cash basis or double entry), the VAT scheme with basis and period of the advance returns, the chart of accounts (SKR 03 or SKR 04), the permanent extension and the state whose public holidays move deadlines. The web app asks the same on its first start; on the command line it is spezado set-up (The command line). Then, in this order: . | Opening balances – what the bank account and the cash held on the first day (The terminal: o on Accounts), so that bank statements close at the balance of the books. | Bank statements – read the files your bank gives you; spezado proposes a booking for every entry. | Documents – read e-invoices into booking proposals, file everything else with the booking it backs. | Reports – the advance VAT returns when they fall due, the Anlage EÜR at the end of the year. | Review – look at the review list now and then; it names what does not fit, in words. | .

18.title: spezado
18.content: Free accounting for everyone – from private finances to freelancers, companies and non-profits. spezado keeps the books of as many organisations as you like, runs on your own device – in the terminal, as a web app or on the command line – and keeps working offline. It is free software (AGPL-3.0-or-later), with every feature included and no telemetry. This is the documentation of version 0.3, a preview: a freelancer’s year in the terminal and in the web app, in German and English. It is not yet for a real tax return – the German mappings (advance VAT return, Anlage EÜR, SKR 03/04) are drafts until tax advisers have reviewed them.

19.title: What 0.3 does
19.content: . | Books for a person: cash basis or double entry, standard VAT or small business, SKR 03 or SKR 04, opening balances; the state whose public holidays move deadlines and the permanent extension of VAT returns. | Bookings from a gross amount and a tax code or in lines; reversals instead of changes; journal, balances and ledgers. | Bank statements from camt.053, MT940 and CSV files, matched to bookings, invoices and earlier payments. | Documents and e-invoices: XRechnung and ZUGFeRD read into booking proposals, other files filed; every original kept by its hash. | Invoices written as XRechnung or ZUGFeRD – with VAT, exempt, under reverse charge, to other EU countries, as exports or as a small business. | Reports: the advance VAT returns with their deadlines, the Anlage EÜR, the HGB statements; closing periods and the GoBD data transfer. | A review list in words: whatever breaks a rule of accounting is shown, never fixed silently. | Synchronisation between a person’s own devices through a relay, end-to-end encrypted, with a recovery code – shared with other people who read or book, keys in the key store of the system (Synchronisation). | In the menu bar with spezado tray, started at login if wished (The web app); the desktop app installs and starts it by itself. | .

22.title: Invoices
22.content: spezado writes invoices as XRechnung 3.0 – an XML file after EN 16931 – or as ZUGFeRD – a PDF to read with the same XRechnung attached for machines (profile XRECHNUNG). Since 2025 businesses in Germany must be able to receive e-invoices (BMF); both formats are e-invoices. The file written is the original: it is kept with the invoice and can be downloaded again.

23.title: Before the first invoice
23.content: . | The seller – your name, address, contact with phone and e-mail, VAT identification number and/or tax number, the IBAN to pay to, the days until payment is due and the prefix of the numbers (terminal: p on Documents). | A customer – name, address, the e-mail invoices go to, the VAT identification number for supplies to businesses abroad or under reverse charge, and the reference a public authority asked for (its Leitweg-ID) (terminal: k). | .

24.title: Writing one
24.content: An invoice has a customer, a date, the day of the supply, lines – what, how much, the unit (hours, days, pieces), the net price and a tax code –, a note and the file to write. Numbers follow in sequence per year: RE-2026-001, RE-2026-002, … On a cash basis the invoice is booked when it is paid – the bank proposes it for the entry that pays it –; with double entry the receivable is booked when the invoice is issued. | Tax code | Category (EN 16931) | What the invoice states | . | de-out-19, de-out-7 | S – 19 % or 7 % |   | . | de-out-0 | Z – 0 % (§ 12 Abs. 3 UStG) |   | . | de-out-exempt | E – exempt (§ 4 UStG) | the reason you give – „Steuerfrei nach § 4 Nr. 14 UStG.“ –, a general one otherwise | . | de-out-13b | AE – reverse charge at home (§ 13b UStG) | „Steuerschuldnerschaft des Leistungsempfängers“ | . | de-out-eu-service | AE – a service to a business in another EU country (§ 3a Abs. 2 UStG) | „Steuerschuldnerschaft des Leistungsempfängers“ | . | de-out-ig-supply | K – intra-Community supply | „Steuerfreie innergemeinschaftliche Lieferung“ | . | de-out-export | G – export | „Steuerfreie Ausfuhrlieferung“ | . | none – small business | E – § 19 UStG | „Gemäß § 19 UStG wird keine Umsatzsteuer berechnet.“ | . The statements are those § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 and § 14a UStG ask for (§ 14a UStG). spezado checks before writing what they need: a customer in Germany for § 13b, a customer in another country for EU services and intra-Community supplies, and the VAT identification numbers of both sides where they must be on the invoice.

25.title: XRechnung and ZUGFeRD
25.content: Both carry the same data and are checked against the rules of XRechnung before they are written. | XRechnung (RE-2026-001.xml, UBL): XML only, as the German public administration receives invoices (XRechnung). | ZUGFeRD (RE-2026-001.pdf) is a PDF/A-3b for people – set in Domitian, with the address in the window of a DIN 5008 envelope – with the XRechnung in CII attached as xrechnung.xml. ZUGFeRD invoices written by spezado pass veraPDF (PDF/A-3b) and the Mustang validator (PDF/A-3b, EN 16931 and XRechnung rules). | . Without a VAT identification number the seller’s tax number is also its identifier (BT-29): EN 16931 requires one of BT-29, BT-30 or BT-31 (rule BR-CO-26). The seller’s details and the customers are part of the books – the owner’s contact and invoicing settings, the customers as organisations – and travel with them to every device. Each device writes invoice numbers in a series of its own, so that two devices offline never write the same number: the first RE-2026-001, the next ones RE-2026-B001, RE-2026-C001 (librotenado 0008). Should two devices ever have taken the same series, the review list says so.

26.title: spezado – design
26.content: The design of spezado: what it is for, how it is built and in what order. The protocol it is built on is specified in librotenado and explained in its whitepaper. Statements marked OPEN are not decided or not verified.

27.title: 1. What it is
27.content: Free accounting for everyone: . | private persons – down to household finances, such as looking at one’s own purchases on one’s own computer; | sole traders and freelancers; | companies – GmbH, AG and other legal forms; | non-profits – associations, foundations, non-profit companies. | . One person has one account and works in as many organisations as they have access to, with roles per organisation (owner, bookkeeper, tax adviser, auditor – OPEN: the final list).

28.title: 2. Principles
28.content: . | Everything included – one edition, every feature free; no paid tiers, licence keys or unlocks. | No telemetry. | Local first – the full core runs on the user’s device and works offline. | Events are the truth – bookings are never changed, only reversed; balances and reports are derived. | librotenado is the model – existing formats are translations; the original document stays the receipt. | Visible conflicts – whatever breaks a rule goes to a review list; nothing is resolved silently. | .

29.title: 3. Scope
29.content: | Area | Content | When | . | Bookkeeping | bookings, accounts, multiple currencies from day one, periods, closing | first | . | Bank | statement import (camt, MT940), then a direct bank connection – early, so that receipts can be matched to real payments | first | . | Receipts | automatic recognition: embedded e-invoice (ZUGFeRD/Factur-X, XRechnung) first, then the text layer, then OCR | first | . | Invoices | writing e-invoices (EN 16931), number ranges per device | first | . | Reports | balances, profit and loss, cash-basis accounts, balance sheet, sphere accounts for non-profits | first | . | Filings | VAT returns and annual filings through adapters (ELSTER/ERiC first) | Germany | . | Payroll | wage tax, social security | Germany, before other countries | . | Other countries | Austria and Switzerland, then further European countries | after Germany is complete | .

30.title: 4. Operation
30.content: One core, three roles, one protocol: . | Client – the full core on a device: standalone, on the command line and in a terminal interface, and behind the open API for the web app and the apps. | Relay – stores and forwards events it cannot read (end-to-end encrypted); anyone can run one for themselves or for others. | Server – a trusted peer that processes plain text: recognition, scheduled bank retrieval, filings, accounts and roles of a team. | .

31.title: 5. Architecture
31.content: . | Rust for the core, the command line and terminal interface, the API, relay and server – one binary. | The open API is the line between spezado and everything around it: HTTP and JSON, described in OpenAPI from the code, with generated clients. A spezado on the same device, in the local network or on a server; devices pair once by code or QR code and get a token each, which can be revoked (OPEN: accounts on servers – passkeys, OIDC). | The web app: Svelte 5 and TypeScript, served by the binary as a static single-page app (TypeScript 6 until Svelte’s tools support TypeScript 7). | Desktop and mobile apps: Flutter, MIT, in their own repository (spezado/apps), talking to spezado through the API only – they contain neither the core nor the librotenado library, and can be distributed through app stores. | Storage: one SQLite database per workspace holds every set of books, so that books that belong together are written in one transaction; originals as files named by their hash. On a server PostgreSQL and S3-compatible storage (OPEN). Archives in open formats; each set of books can be exported and imported on its own. | Books stay apart: one set of books per organisation or person – the unit of sharing and encryption. A business transaction across books (a bill partly private) is one booking in each, linked by a transaction (librotenado 0002) and written together. | Synchronisation: a growing set of events, hybrid logical clocks, a hash chain per device, a review list (librotenado 0002); encryption for groups after librotenado 0006. | . Crates . | Crate | Content | . | spezado-core | the books over librotenado’s event set; commands checked into events; journal and review list – pure, no I/O | . | spezado-law | the interface of law modules: facts of an owner in, charts, tax codes, reports and periods out | . | spezado-law-de | German law | . | spezado-store | events in SQLite, originals as files | . | spezado-app | the workspace: stamping, storing and applying commands all or none, workflows, reports, export and import | . | spezado-tui, spezado-api | the terminal interface and the API, through spezado-app only | . | spezado | the binary: the command line, tui, serve | .

32.title: 6. Law as modules
32.content: . | Building blocks instead of one module per country: country × legal form × additions (non-profit, small business) × region. | Pure functions: facts in – who the owner is and how it keeps its books (librotenado 0008) –, derived results out (charts, tax codes, reports, periods, deadlines); no I/O, no state. | Data before code: rates, charts of accounts and form mappings are tables with validity periods, published by librotenado. | Versions per period: closing a period records the modules and versions its figures were derived with. | Rust, built two ways: spezado’s European modules are compiled in; external modules are loaded as WebAssembly components in a sandbox (OPEN). | Never proprietary: the module interface is AGPL; a module declares its licence and source in a manifest and must be free software compatible with the AGPL. | Tested against official cases (ERiC test data, wage tax test tables, XRechnung examples) and reviewed by someone who knows the law, not only the code – all German mappings by tax advisers before the first stable release. | .

35.title: 9. State
35.content: Milestone 5, first stage – a person’s own devices, after librotenado 0006: . | spezado relay holds, per set of books, the ordered member list and the envelopes of events and originals, and checks signatures, the rules of the member list and who may write – never content. It speaks HTTP behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS. | A device starts synchronising books: it founds their member list with itself and a recovery code – shown once, for paper – and sends every event and original, encrypted with the books key. | Another device of the person joins with an invitation (relay, books, a secret; good for a day); the inviting device adds it at its next synchronisation, after checking the proof. The new device unwraps the key and the chain and receives everything. | When every device is lost, the recovery code recovers the books onto a new one. | spezado serve synchronises every minute; the terminal with y, the command line with spezado sync. | Second stage: other people with rights (read, write, manage) by invitation, removing a device or a person (the key changes), read-only books refuse commands; seeds in the key store of the system; the seller’s details, customers and series of invoice numbers per device as events (librotenado 0.6); serve --listen for other devices over TLS with a certificate of the workspace’s own, its fingerprint in the pairing link and a QR code. | OPEN: access for a limited time, an auditor for one period. | . Version 0.1.0, a preview – for trying out, not for a real tax return: the German mappings are drafts until tax advisers have reviewed them. On top of milestones 0 to 3 (version 0.2.0 adds milestone 5, above): . | Opening balances, booked once against the opening balance sheet (librotenado 0004), so that statements close at the books’ balance; balances carry on between years by themselves. | VAT deadlines move on public holidays of the state where the tax office sits (§ 108 Abs. 3 AO; holidays of only some municipalities left out) and by a month with the permanent extension (§ 46 UStDV); both are part of the configuration (librotenado 0008) and can be changed from a date on, in the terminal, the API and the web app. OPEN: whether the current AEAO to § 108 names the seat of the tax office. | Payments booked before their statement: the first proposal for an entry; accepting it reverses the booking and books it again on the statement’s bank account, naming the entry, on the same day. | Invoices written as XRechnung 3.0 (UBL) or as ZUGFeRD (profile XRECHNUNG): a PDF/A-3b set in Domitian with the XRechnung in CII attached, accepted by veraPDF and the Mustang validator; the file written is the original kept. The seller’s details, customers, numbers in sequence per year, lines at 19, 7 or 0 % VAT, exempt (§ 4 UStG, with the reason), under reverse charge at home (§ 13b UStG) or as a service to a business in another EU country (§ 3a Abs. 2 UStG), intra-Community supplies and exports – each with the statement § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 and § 14a UStG ask for and the VAT identification numbers they need –, or as a small business (§ 19 UStG); booked when paid on a cash basis, when issued with double entry. Without a VAT identification number the seller’s tax number is also its identifier (BT-29): EN 16931 requires BT-29, BT-30 or BT-31 (BR-CO-26, fatal). The seller’s details and customers travel with the books; every device writes its own series of numbers. | The review list in words, German and English: each issue names the booking, document, entry and amount. | Releases: binaries for Linux (x86_64, arm64), macOS (arm64) and Windows (x86_64) with the web app embedded. | . Milestone 3: spezado serve – the open API on the device itself, described in api/openapi.json: pairing, books and their set-up, overview, journal, accounts, balances, tax codes, bookings from a gross amount and in lines, reversals, documents (read with a booking proposal, filed with or without a booking, the original fetched again), bank statements and their open entries (booked by hand, by a proposal, all proposals at once; FinTS answers 501 until registered), reports, the review list, closing, the GoBD export as a ZIP, and Server-Sent Events when something changed. And the web app, served by the same binary, with all of it: pairing by the address spezado serve shows, setting up books, overview, journal, bank, documents, accounts with their ledger, reports with a CSV download, the review list and closing – German and English, light and dark, live when the books change. Next: the Flutter apps (M4) – they need the API from other devices, with TLS. Milestone 2: the tab Bank – statements read from files in camt.053, MT940 or a bank’s CSV, a bank account opened for each IBAN, statements read twice and entries two statements show left out; each entry booked from its gross amount with an account and a tax code, or by a proposal: the unbooked invoice it pays, or the account of the same party’s last entry; all proposals at once. The review list shows entries booked twice and statements that do not close at their account’s balance. Fetching from the bank (FinTS) is a placeholder: it needs a product registration with the Deutsche Kreditwirtschaft, which falkOSS applies for once it is founded (OPEN). Milestone 1: the terminal interface (spezado tui), in German and English, by keyboard and mouse – setting up a freelancer’s books (cash basis or double entry, standard or small-business VAT, SKR 03 or 04), booking from a gross amount and a tax code or in lines, reversing, reading e-invoices (XRechnung, ZUGFeRD) into booking proposals and filing other documents, balances and ledgers, the advance VAT returns with their deadlines and the Anlage EÜR, the review list, closing periods and the data transfer of the GoBD (Z3). OPEN: reading the text layer and photos of documents. Milestone 0: spezado init, set-up, book, reverse, journal, balance, report, close, check, export and import on a workspace. German reports as librotenado publishes them: the VAT return of 2026, the Anlage EÜR of 2025 and 2026, the HGB statements of 2026.

37.title: Synchronisation
37.content: A set of books starts on one device. Through a relay it reaches the person’s other devices – end-to-end encrypted after librotenado 0006: every device encrypts what it sends with the key of the books, which only the devices of the books hold. The relay stores and passes on what it cannot read. It sees which books it holds, which device sends when and how much, and the names of the devices – not the books. Books are shared the same way with other people – a tax adviser who reads, a bookkeeper who books –, each with what they may do.

38.title: Starting
38.content: On the device that holds the books: . spezado sync start https://relay.example.org --name Laptop . spezado founds the books’ member list on the relay – this device and a recovery code – and sends every event and original. It prints the recovery code once: 53 characters in groups of four. Write it down and keep it safe. If every device is lost, it brings the books back to a new one; without it and without a device, the books are lost. In the terminal it is y on Overview, in the web app the panel Synchronisation on the overview.

39.title: Another device
39.content: On the device that holds the books, make an invitation – good for a day: . spezado sync invite # https://relay.example.org#join=01a1….rm-H3_gG… . On the new device – a workspace of its own, with a device name the books do not have yet: . spezado init --device phone spezado sync join 'https://relay.example.org#join=01a1…' --name Phone . The next synchronisation on the first device adds it – it checks that the request was made with its invitation –, and the next one on the new device brings the books. spezado serve synchronises every minute by itself; the web app offers join when setting up, the terminal shows the invitation with v on Overview. spezado sync # every set of books that is synchronised spezado sync devices # the devices of the books .

40.title: Other people and what they may do
40.content: An invitation says what the device it brings may do: . | Rights |   | . | manage | everything: read, book, invite and remove – the person’s own devices (the default) | . | write | read and book – a bookkeeper | . | read | only read – a tax adviser; on such a device, spezado refuses to book | . spezado sync invite --rights read # for the tax adviser . The web app offers the same when inviting and shows what every device may do.

41.title: Removing a device or a person
41.content: spezado sync remove Steuerberaterin # by name or device name . The books get a new key, which the device removed does not receive: nothing written afterwards reaches it. What it has read, it may have kept – removing protects the future, not the past. In the web app, every device but this one has remove.

42.title: Where the keys are
42.content: Each device keeps its key of the books in the key store of the system – the macOS keychain, the Windows credential manager, the Secret Service on Linux. Where there is none – a server, a container –, or with SPEZADO_KEYCHAIN=0, it stays in the workspace; spezado sync start says which. Protect the workspace’s folder then.

43.title: Recovery
43.content: When no device is left: . spezado init --device tablet spezado --books 01a1… sync recover https://relay.example.org WFXE-TNQP-… . The recovery code adds the new device to the books, which then receives everything. Keep the identity of the books with the code – spezado books shows it.

44.title: Running a relay
44.content: A relay is the same program: . spezado relay --data /var/lib/spezado-relay --listen 127.0.0.1:8049 . Or as a container – every release after 0.3.0 is also an image for Linux on amd64 and arm64, ghcr.io/spezado/spezado, which runs the relay unless told otherwise. With deploy/compose.yaml next to you and the version of a release: . SPEZADO_VERSION=0.4.0 docker compose up -d # the version of the release to run . It speaks HTTP and is meant to run behind a reverse proxy that speaks TLS, at the root of its address. With Caddy, which fetches certificates by itself: . relay.example.org { reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8049 } . The relay keeps its data in one SQLite database. It accepts new books from anyone who founds them, and from then on only what their members sign; a request to join waits at most a day.

45.title: The terminal
45.content: spezado tui starts the terminal interface. It works with the keyboard and the mouse: every key shown at the bottom is also a button, rows can be clicked and scrolled. With the mouse on, selecting text needs the modifier key of your terminal; m switches the mouse off.

46.title: Moving around
46.content: | Key |   | . | 1 … 8, Tab, Shift-Tab | the tabs: Overview, Journal, Bank, Documents, Accounts, Reports, Review, Closing | . | ↑ ↓ | the rows of a tab | . | ↵ | open the row: a bank entry to book, an account’s ledger, a report | . | [ ] | the year before, the year after | . | s | German or English | . | m | mouse on or off | . | q, Ctrl-C | quit | . In a form, ↵, Tab or ↓ go to the next field and ↵ on the last one confirms; Shift-Tab or ↑ go back, ← → change a choice and Esc cancels. An account field searches as you type – by number or name – and ↵ takes the account picked with ↑ ↓. Amounts and dates are written as in the language shown: 1.234,50 and 29.10.2026 in German, 1,234.50 and 2026-10-29 in English. Accounts are given by their number in your chart (4930) – or, for a bank account, by its IBAN.

47.title: The tabs
47.content: | Tab | Keys |   | . | Overview | n new booking, i read a document, d deadlines, y synchronise (or set it up), v invite a device | bank and cash, income, expenses and result of the year, the next advance VAT return and when it is due, open entries, review, the date closed up to, and the relay the books are synchronised through | . | Journal | n new booking, z booking in lines, r reverse | every booking; a reversal refers to what it cancels – nothing is changed or deleted | . | Bank | i read a statement, ↵ book, a book all proposals, f fetch | the entries of your statements not booked yet, each with a proposal where spezado found one | . | Documents | i read, n new booking, r write an invoice, k new customer, p seller | documents with their originals | . | Accounts | ↵ ledger, o opening balances | the balance of every account | . | Reports | ↵ open, then e export as CSV, p prepare as a filing; ↵ on a filing submits it or asks where it stands | the reports that apply to the year, then the filings (Filings) | . | Review |   | what needs review, in words | . | Closing | c close a period, g GoBD data transfer |   | . A new booking (n) is date, text, account, gross amount, tax code and payment from the bank or the cash: spezado books the net amount, the VAT and the payment. A booking in lines (z) takes lines of account=amount[@code], separated by spaces, positive for debit and negative for credit: 4930=10,00@de-in-19 1576=1,90 1200=-11,90. Deadlines (d): the state whose public holidays move deadlines (§ 108 Abs. 3 AO) and the permanent extension of advance VAT returns (§ 46 UStDV), from a date on. Bank proposals come in this order: a payment booked before the statement came (it is booked again on the statement’s bank account, naming the entry), the invoice the entry pays, and the same party’s last entry. A proposal is only a proposal: ↵ shows it to confirm or change. Fetching from the bank (f) needs a registration as a FinTS product, which spezado does not have yet – read the statement files your bank gives you instead. Opening balances (o): per account account=amount, holdings positive and debts negative – 1200=3.160,50 1000=200. They are booked once, against the opening balance sheet, and carry on from year to year by themselves.

48.title: The web app
48.content: spezado serve serves the web app and the API on this device, at http://127.0.0.1:8048 (another port with --port). Nothing is loaded from elsewhere – no fonts, no scripts, no tracking. spezado serve # spezado serves at http://127.0.0.1:8048 # Pair a device with the code 6958d36774 – or open http://127.0.0.1:8048/#pair=6958d36774 .

49.title: In the menu bar
49.content: spezado tray runs the same server with an icon in the menu bar (macOS) or the system tray (Windows): Open spezado opens the web app, Pair a device … makes a new pairing code and opens the pairing link, Start at login starts it whenever you log in, Quit spezado stops it. Like serve, it creates the workspace if there is none. The release builds have it on macOS and Windows; on Linux, spezado serve runs without an icon. On Windows, started at login, it still keeps a console window open (OPEN). spezado tray spezado autostart on # start at login: `tray` where there is one, else `serve`; `off` to stop, none to ask . Apps that start spezado themselves give it the pairing code in SPEZADO_PAIRING_CODE – at least 16 letters, digits, - or _ – and pair with it at once.

50.title: Other devices
50.content: To reach spezado from a phone, a tablet or an app in the same network, let it listen there – only over TLS: . spezado serve --listen 0.0.0.0:8443 --host laptop.local . It makes a certificate of the workspace’s own for the host name and keeps it. The pairing link carries the certificate’s fingerprint and is printed as a QR code: an app checks the fingerprint, a browser asks once whether to trust the certificate. A server with a domain can put a reverse proxy with a certificate of its own in front instead (Synchronisation, running a relay).

51.title: Pairing
51.content: Every browser is paired once: open the address with #pair=… that serve shows, or enter the code on the page. The code is valid for a quarter of an hour and for one device; a new start of serve shows a new one. The browser keeps the token it receives; another browser needs a code of its own.

52.title: The pages
52.content: | Page |   | . | Overview | bank and cash, income, expenses and result of the year, the next advance VAT return and when it is due; the state and the permanent extension that move deadlines, changed from a date on; synchronisation – starting it, the devices, inviting one, synchronising now (Synchronisation) | . | Journal | every booking, reversals | . | Bank | read statements, book entries or accept the proposals | . | Documents | read e-invoices into booking proposals, file other documents, download every original | . | Invoices | the seller’s details, customers, invoices written as XRechnung or ZUGFeRD (Invoices) | . | Accounts | balances, ledgers, opening balances | . | Reports | the reports of the year, as CSV, too; the filings prepared from them (Filings) | . | Review | what needs review, in words | . | Closing | closing periods, the GoBD data transfer | . Without books, the web app sets up new ones – or brings them from another device, with an invitation or the recovery code. While serve runs, it synchronises every minute. + Buchen / + Book books from a gross amount or in lines. The language (German, English) and light or dark – or like the system – are chosen at the top and kept in the browser. What another browser, the terminal or the command line writes shows up at once.
